title: Why do we get brain freeze?
sources: Wake Forest Baptist Medical Center Neuroscience

lines.text: Why does eating ice cream too fast trigger a stabbing headache behind your eyes?
lines.caps: Why does eating ice cream *fast | cause *brain freeze?

lines.text: The medical name is sphenopalatine ganglioneuralgia, and your brain isn't actually freezing at all.
When cold slush hits the roof of your mouth, it rapidly cools sensitive blood vessels at the palate.
lines.caps: Cold slush chills *blood vessels | in the roof of your *mouth

lines.text: To protect your brain from temperature shock, these arteries violently constrict and then flood with warm blood.
lines.caps: Arteries rapidly dilate to *flood | the area with warm *blood

lines.text: This sudden surge triggers pain receptors in the trigeminal nerve, which also senses facial pain.
Your brain gets confused by the nerve signals, mistakenly feeling the pain in your forehead and eyes.
lines.caps: Your brain mistakes the *pain | as coming from your *forehead!

lines.text: To stop it instantly, press your warm tongue flat against the roof of your mouth.
lines.caps: Press your warm *tongue | to the roof of your *mouth!
